assessments.evidence: The edition overview says Essentials Cloud only where available and Premier Cloud/CMP. The regional assistant compatibility distinguishes Cloud 8.2+ from CMP 8.8+. For agentic CMP, the setup adds Platform 10.4+, ES 8.8+, Cloud Connect 2.0+ and SAIA 2.4+. The current SAIA 2.4 installer additionally requires qualifying paid license, fresh setup, outbound 443, STC/OAuth signing certificate, administrator capabilities, verified license-domain email and supported AWS commercial region. Preserve older 2.3.6 incompatibility/planned-release wording as historical.
assessments.qualification: Assistant edition, entitlement, Cloud/CMP and exact enablement prerequisites.

assessments.evidence: The current authoring task requires Cloud Platform 10.1+/ES 8.6+ or CMP Platform 10.4+/ES 8.8+/Cloud Connect 2.0+, with the agentic setup adding SAIA 2.4+. Both editions are listed. Finding-based detection is turned off in 8.8. Agent can advise on SPL, validation and troubleshooting but cannot save, clone, change version/status or test the detection.
assessments.qualification: Detection Builder Cloud/CMP, version, edition, stage and setup prerequisites.

assessments.evidence: The aggregate is Essentials/Premier Cloud only. The detailed response-plan guide requires AI Assistant enablement and view/edit response-template permissions, while JSON importing remains independent. The upload list includes ZIP and Considerations omits it. Preserve that conflict, 50 MB/text-only conditions, and review suggested actions/SPL against actual paired SOAR capabilities.
assessments.qualification: SOP deployment, edition and Assistant dependency.

assessments.evidence: The current canonical card and task retain Premier Cloud, ES 8.8+ and alpha status independent of product GA. At least one risk-based detection and approximately one million processed events are required before findings. Representative enablement and test-queue behavior remain explicit.
assessments.qualification: Threat Graph documented stage, prerequisites, eligibility and enablement.

assessments.evidence: Triage and Autonomous Response have distinct table rows and stages. Cloud table Platform 10.2+/ES 8.6+ conflicts with linked 8.8 task ES 8.7+. Triage supports Cloud/CMP; CA Response has a Cloud-only availability cell with CMP compatibility bullets. The parent limits 200 analyses/tenant/day and 20 revisions/investigation/day conflict with linked first-ten, approximately 200 findings/day and no-rerun guidance. Response cannot rerun or process later findings and requires frontier models. Asset-role and connector/action access, paired SOAR, enablement and exact region remain explicit.
assessments.qualification: SOC workflow stage, edition, paired dependencies, limits, model and asset or connector permissions. Keep current and historical guide conflicts scoped.

scopeOutcomes.qualification: The workflow matrix was compared by edition and release. The 8.8 agent aggregate gives Guided Response to Essentials and Premier on Cloud and Cloud Connected CMP, with Platform 10.2+, ES 8.6+ and paired SOAR. Its historical 8.6 task remains Cloud-scoped and the 8.7 matrix assigns enhancements to Premier. The 8.7 Connector Builder aggregate lists both editions but the 8.7.1 release enhancement says Premier. Malware/Phishing aggregate says ES 8.5+, while the detailed task requires Platform 10.2+/ES 8.6+ and paired SOAR. Automation Builder and Connector Builder task floors, permissions and pairings remain independent. UEBA behavior/product description supports the maintained Premier capability. App for SOAR 8.8.0 matrix still contains literal 8..0 for an on-premises combination. Export Cloud and Enterprise separately require Python 3.13, proper roles/ports and tested combinations, with CIM 8.5.0-1681. Additional Splunkbase versions are for upgrade listing purposes. Neither package numbering nor license proves a pairing. The 8.8.1 Export note fixes PAPP-38632 without silently broadening the tested scope. The current 8.8 compatibility prose repeats TAXII 2.0; the 8.2 introduction names 2.0 and 2.1 while its compatibility section names 1.0 and 1.1. The native feed procedure and TIM Cloud authentication change are separate. The canonical discrepancy retains these statements without choosing an unsupported protocol version.

issueObservations.rationale: The 8.7 aggregate still includes both editions while the 8.7.1 release enhancement says Premier. Current 8.8 wording does not settle the earlier same-version edition conflict.

The 8.8 aggregate now lists both editions on Cloud and Cloud Connected CMP. The 8.7 matrix groups enhancements under Premier and the old 8.6 task is Cloud-scoped. Preserve exact historical and enhancement scope.
The reviewed 8.8 aggregate says ES 8.5+ but the detailed task says Platform 10.2+/ES 8.6+ with paired SOAR. The stricter task minimum stays explicit.
The reviewed App for SOAR tested matrix still contains literal 8..0. Export prerequisite rows are a separate explicit package matrix and cannot repair that malformed value.
The pricing overview lists multiple models, while the detailed activity FAQ is scoped to Cloud Platform. ES deployment and individual contract eligibility need their own evidence.

The current table identifies Triage as Premier, with Cloud and CMP prerequisites. Retain corrected older lower-edition wording as history. Pairing, activation, exact region and customer entitlement stay unresolved independently.
The 8.8 aggregate lists Cloud ES 8.6+ whereas the linked Triage and Autonomous Response tasks require 8.7+. Neither the parent credit explanation nor product GA resolves those floors.
Autonomous Response availability says Premier Cloud only while the compatibility bullets and detailed task provide a CMP minimum. Keep the CMP availability intersection unresolved.

The parent describes 200 analyses per tenant per day and 20 revisions per investigation per day. The linked task still says first ten findings, approximately 200 findings per day and no rerun. Same-version disagreement remains explicit.
The separate Response task disallows rerun and later-added findings and requires frontier models. The Triage revision model does not clear this independent component limitation.

The official 8.8 license guide describes working Cloud Connected features during a Premier trial with the UI showing Essentials until a paid license is applied. Retain both the operation and display scopes alongside expiry restrictions.

The current Threat Graph task requires at least one risk-based detection and approximately one million events before producing findings. The current report includes that prerequisite alongside Premier Cloud and alpha-stage qualifications.

The 8.8 compatibility text repeats TAXII 2.0. The 8.2 feature introduction names 2.0 and 2.1 while its compatibility passage names 1.0 and 1.1. Native feed protocol, STIX parsing and TIM Cloud authentication remain separate; the current public discrepancy preserves these qualifications.
